title: A 'name must be at least 2 characters' rule rejects a real, single-letter surname
assumption: No legitimate name is only one character long.

input.description: A form validator's minimum-length rule applied to a surname field.

what_goes_wrong: A person whose surname genuinely is a single letter is rejected by a length check that has nothing to do with whether the name is real — it's purely a guess about how short a name 'should' be.
why: Single-character surnames exist in multiple naming traditions (for example, several Korean surnames romanize to a single letter), and a minimum-length rule has no way to distinguish a genuinely short name from a placeholder like "x" someone typed to get past the form. The rule enforces an assumption about length that is simply false for this input, not a check that catches bad data.

repros.expected_output:
Yu True
O rejected: name must be at least 2 characters

Yu true
O rejected: name must be at least 2 characters

fix: Don't impose a minimum name length unless you have a specific, documented reason to; if you need to catch empty or placeholder input, check for that directly (empty string, all the same character) rather than guessing a length threshold.

sources.title: Patrick McKenzie: Falsehoods Programmers Believe About Names

test_cases.note: A real single-letter surname should not be rejected purely on length.
